question.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -4 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & 16 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & 16\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}9-\lambda  & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & 16-\lambda  & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & 16-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (16-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}9-\lambda  & -12 \\ -12 & 16-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (16-\lambda )((9-\lambda )(16-\lambda )-144) & =0 \\ (16-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda -16\lambda +144-144) & =0 \\ (16-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-25\lambda ) & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -16)(\lambda -25) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =25,\,16,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{25}=5 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{16}=4 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$
